title: Was that word on the list?
hook: A word feels familiar. How can you check where it came from?

knows: a list contains some words and not others
doesNotKnow: that a plausible or familiar-feeling word need not have appeared in a specific list

misconception: A word that feels familiar must have appeared on the list.
objective: Compare a probe word against the original list, distinguishing familiarity from evidence about its source.

claims.text: The Rest list consists of bed, rest, awake, dream and night; the probe sleep is absent. The Desk list consists of paper, pencil, ruler, eraser and pen; the probe pencil is present.
claims.source: The authored CASES fixture in src/demos/psychology/was-that-word-on-the-list/Demo.tsx; the membership is computed from the same array displayed on screen.

claims.text: A word can fit the theme without appearing in that list; comparing each probe to the source settles membership for the two authored lists.
claims.source: The Rest example is the counterexample; compare the probe sleep with its authored list in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: Familiarity and a trace of where you saw something are different kinds of information. A feeling of familiarity alone does not establish that a word appeared on a particular list.
claims.source: OpenStax Psychology 2e, 8.3 Problems with Memory, https://openstax.org/books/psychology-2e/pages/8-3-problems-with-memory (source monitoring and misattribution); independent checking of the wording and source is pending.

claims.text: The short activity illustrates source checking; it does not test or diagnose the learner's memory ability.
claims.source: This single, uncontrolled authored activity in Demo.tsx is not a validated assessment.

claims.text: In the recall example, the word sea is not present in the original list tide, wave, coast, sand.
claims.source: Authored recall fixture below: membership by direct comparison.

recall.question: A list was tide, wave, coast, sand. Later the word sea feels familiar. What establishes whether sea was on that list?
recall.why: The source list has tide, wave, coast and sand; sea is not one of its words. Feeling familiar is not proof that it appeared there.
